subject: TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD function
notes: cite.py --check 15.90.2 "TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD" => OK (General format, FUNCTION and TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD both underlined = required, one parenthesized argument-1, no brackets anywhere). READ: CobolExpressions.g4#functionReference `FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*` with `functionName : IDENTIFIER | DISPLAY | LENGTH | MERGE | NATIONAL | BIT | RANDOM | SIGN | SORT | SUM` — TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD is not a reserved word so it lexes IDENTIFIER and the format parses; the lexer's FUNCTION suppression keeps the '(' in the argument region (SR6) so 20240229 is an argument, not a subscript. READ: IntrinsicCatalog.cs line 274 `Add(new("TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD", IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1, "i", "TestDateYyyymmdd", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, false, 2002))` — Fixed 1..1 makes the parenthesized single argument MANDATORY: the grammar's optional arg-list and the empty-parens form both reach IntrinsicBinder.cs:573 with given=0 and raise COBOL1504 "takes 1 argument(s); 0 given (ISO §15.3)", so the no-argument shape the format does not offer is rejected. IntrinsicType.Integer matches §15.90.1 "The type of this function is integer" and Table 21 line 29995 (Int1 -> Int). EDITIONS derived from the spec, NOT from the catalog row: Annex E item 13 (line 42993) enumerates the intrinsic functions NEW in 2023 (BASECONVERT, CONCAT, CONVERT, FIND-STRING, MODULE-NAME, SMALLEST-ALGEBRAIC, SUBSTITUTE) and TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD is absent, so it predates 2023; it is not in the COBOL-85 + Amendment-1 intrinsic set, and D.31.3.8 presents it in the 2002 date-function family — hence 2002,2014,2023. The edition gate is live and pinned: conformance:cases/15.93.4-Returned-value-rule/test_validators_below_2002 carries `reject-at: 85` and expects COBOL1502 (IntrinsicBinder.cs:494 "was introduced by ISO/IEC 1989:{sig.IntroducedIn}"). Positive golden intrinsics_test_validators writes the format seven times and is registered in tests/conformance/2002/manifest.json and ConformanceTests.cs:179. || REFUTED: VERDICT SURVIVES — CONFORMS confirmed, but the record's EDITIONS EVIDENCE is corrected and one over-claim in the note is withdrawn. (1) Citation re-derived independently: cite.py --check 15.90.2 "TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD" => OK, §15.90.2 (General format), text `<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD</u> ( argument-1 )` — both words underlined, no bracketed element, exactly one argument. (2) The grammar claim was NOT taken on trust: CobolExpressions.g4:333 is verbatim `FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*`, and the FNARG re-typing is real — CobolLexer.g4:14 `tokens { FNARG_LPAREN, FNARG_RPAREN }` and CobolLexer.g4:119 `if (PreviousIsFunctionName()) Type = FNARG_LPAREN;` — so §8.4.3.2.3 SR6 is mechanically enforced, not asserted. (3) The arity gate was read at source, not quoted: IntrinsicBinder.cs `long given = args.Sum(...)` then `if (given < sig.MinArgs || given > sig.MaxArgs) ctx.Edition.Error("COBOL1504", ...)`, sitting AFTER BindIntrinsicArgs and BEFORE every per-function arm; and `grep TEST-DATE IntrinsicBinder.cs` returns NOTHING, so there is no bespoke arm that could divert this row past the gate. Both halves of the format (accept the one shape it offers / reject the shapes it does not) are therefore verified. (4) ⛔ EDITIONS — RULE 4 HAZARD, PARTIALLY REALIZED. Annex E item 13 is real and I re-read it (lines 42993–43001: BASECONVERT, CONCAT, CONVERT, FIND-STRING, MODULE-NAME, SMALLEST-ALGEBRAIC, SUBSTITUTE), so the UPPER bound ("predates 2023") IS spec-derived. The LOWER bound is NOT. The note's two supports for 2002 do not carry it: "not in the COBOL-85 + Amendment-1 intrinsic set" is asserted with no citation and no --check, and D.31.3.8 (line 42650, re-read in full) is informative prose about the verdict codes that makes NO edition statement whatsoever — it neither says nor implies 2002. The 2023 transcription's Annex E records the delta from 2014 ONLY, so the 2002-vs-2014-vs-85 boundary is not derivable from `specs/ISO_COBOL.md` at all. The value 2002 is left standing because it is very likely correct and the rule-4 fallback ("85,2002,2014,2023") would be affirmatively WORSE — it would assert availability in an edition the function demonstrably post-dates — but it is recorded here as NOT spec-derived, and it coincides exactly with the `2002` field of the IntrinsicCatalog row under review, which is the shape rule 4 exists to catch. If the edition gate is ever challenged, the evidence must come from the 2002 or 2014 edition's own annex, not from this transcription.
